item.title: Keel (KEEL) Sells Entire Bitcoin Treasury for $192 Million, Will Sell BTC Daily
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Keel (KEEL) Sells Entire Bitcoin Treasury for $192 Million, Will Sell BTC Daily Keel Infrastructure sold its entire bitcoin treasury in the third quarter, offloading 2,520 bitcoin for $192 million and leaving the company with only nominal holdings at Sept. 30, the former Bitfarms miner reported Thursday. The sales covered the 2,261 bitcoin Keel held going into the quarter plus the 259 it mined, and the company said it timed them during periods of strength. Going forward, bitcoin mined from Keel’s remaining Quebec operations will be sold on a daily basis, “effectively eliminating the Company’s exposure to Bitcoin price movements on treasury holdings.” The move completes a shift Keel began earlier this year, when the company, then still trading as Bitfarms (BITF), started selling its stack and winding down U.S. mining to fund high-performance computing and AI infrastructure. From bitcoin miner to AI landlord Keel Infrastructure Corp. rebranded from Bitfarms after completing a U.S. redomiciliation to Delaware in April and now describes itself as a North American digital infrastructure and energy company. Legacy bitcoin mining still shows up in the results, but the center of gravity has moved. Revenue from continuing operations fell to $28 million from $68 million a year earlier, largely because Keel stopped U.S. bitcoin mining in the second quarter and because the average bitcoin price declined. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a negative $27 million from a positive $19 million. General and administrative expenses roughly doubled to $34 million as the company hired senior specialists and booked higher stock-based compensation. The company still posted about $780 million of unrestricted cash as of Nov. 4 and said it has no current need for debt or equity financing before signing a lease. “Power supply is getting scarcer while demand keeps climbing,” CEO Ben Gagnon said in the release. “Keel’s 2027 and 2028 power is further advanced, more secure, and closer to delivery than it was last quarter.” CFO Jonathan Mir added that capital deployed ahead of a lease becomes equity in project financing and that the company examines opportunities to recycle capital on an ongoing basis. What Keel is building instead Construction began at Moses Lake in September after Keel cleared Notice to Proceed, and the company expects it to be the first energized site generating HPC revenue in 2027. It also engineered an optional plan for next-generation Vera Rubin architecture at the site. Permitting advanced at Sharon and Panther Creek in Pennsylvania, and load studies could expand secured data center capacity from 478 MW toward nearly 1.9 GW if Panther Creek and Scrubgrass expansions proceed. Keel has also moved to consolidate older bitcoin sites into a single AI campus. item.title: U.S.-Sanctioned Moscow Exchange Will List Bitcoin on Dec. 1 as Russia Pulls Crypto Trading Home
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S.-Sanctioned Moscow Exchange Will List Bitcoin on Dec. 1 as Russia Pulls Crypto Trading Home Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, will begin trading bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT on Dec. 1, the exchange announced this week, calling it the country’s first organized market for digital currencies. The launch puts bitcoin on the same screens Russians use to trade Sberbank and Gazprom shares. It also puts a major crypto venue inside an institution that sits under U.S. sanctions. The first phase will run as a pilot. Participants will connect as they are ready, and the exchange said interest has come from existing members, their clients and businesses that already use digital currencies for investment and settlement. How the Moscow market will work Trading will run on the exchange’s existing stock market technology and follow its stock market hours, from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, the exchange told Russian newspaper Vedomosti. The National Clearing Centre, the exchange’s clearing arm, will clear every trade. From day one, clients can settle trades the same day or the next day, and the exchange will offer swaps to help participants manage liquidity. BTC, ETH and USDT will trade in both addressed and addressless modes, and the list is set to grow over time with Russian and international instruments. Custody will run through partner digital depositaries, a new type of entity created under the country’s rules. A Moscow Exchange executive first previewed the plan on Oct. 31. Retail access is tight. Non-qualified investors must pass a test before they can buy, and they can purchase no more than 300,000 rubles of digital currency a year, roughly $3,700, through a single broker. Qualified investors face no cap. The exchange had first flagged plans to debut bitcoin trading in October. For the exchange, the structure keeps crypto inside a regime it already runs. Brokers connect the way they do for equities, trades net through the same clearing system and investor classifications carry over from the stock market. That lowers the barrier for banks and brokerages that want to offer bitcoin without building separate custody and matching systems of their own. Sanctions loom over USDT The U.S. Treasury blocked Moscow Exchange and the National Clearing Centre in June 2024 as part of a broader push against Russia’s financial system over the war in Ukraine. That makes the clearing house holding customers’ USDT a sanctioned entity. Tether routinely freezes wallets tied to addresses on the Treasury’s sanctions list, which raises questions about how the stablecoin issuer would treat USDT held through the Moscow clearing structure. Neither the exchange nor Tether has publicly addressed that issue. The choice of USDT, a dollar-pegged token, is notable for a market built in part to operate outside the dollar system. item.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout Wipes Out Leveraged Longs
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout Wipes Out Leveraged Longs Bitcoin price fell about 5% on Thursday morning, sliding from above $80,800 to near $76,000 as a sharp selloff in technology stocks spread into crypto and wiped out leveraged traders betting on further gains, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The drop erased the rebound that had carried bitcoin back above $80,000 overnight. It touched a low near $76,100 shortly after the U.S. stock market opened, its weakest level since the start of the week. The reversal came fast. Bitcoin held near $80,000 through Wednesday, and early Thursday traders were cheering a short squeeze that pushed it past $80,500. Within roughly two hours of the opening bell, the bitcoin price was more than $4,000 lower. Wall Street’s AI trade breaks The trigger sat on Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled as much as 3.9% on Thursday and slipped into correction territory, trading 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 fell about 2%, erasing Wednesday’s rally, its best session in three months. Chip and AI stocks took the worst of it. Nvidia and Broadcom each fell about 5%, Tesla lost around 9% and neocloud names CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN dropped between 9% and 13%. Qualcomm slid 9% after a weak outlook. Sandisk was down nearly 19% at the time of writing. Investors are pricing in a Democratic-controlled Congress after Tuesday’s midterms. Traders fear new limits on the data center buildout, and UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of U.S. data center capacity additions expected in 2028 could be at risk from construction pauses, Reuters reported. The selling started in Asia, where South Korea’s Kospi closed down more than 5% as Samsung and SK hynix sank. U.S. stocks shed $2.3 trillion in market value within the first hour of trading, with the Russell 2000 plunging 2.5% and on pace for its biggest one-day drop since June 5 Bitcoin price has traded alongside that AI-heavy tech complex for most of the year, and bitcoin miners are now part of it. Many have sold bitcoin to fund AI data centers, so the same political risk now weighs on both. Leverage unwinds Leverage turned the move into a flush. Roughly $370 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in about an hour as bitcoin broke $77,000 and ether fell below $2,300, most of them long bets. Wider tallies circulating on X put long liquidations closer to $400 million over the same 60 minutes. The U.S. stock market shed more than $1 trillion in value within minutes of the open, and crypto went with it. Wednesday’s short squeeze had pulled in late buyers with borrowed money. When stocks broke, those positions were the first to go, and forced selling pushed the bitcoin price through support around $77,000. item.title: Ukraine Central Bank Refuses to Back Crypto Bill Cleared for Second Reading
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Ukraine Central Bank Refuses to Back Crypto Bill Cleared for Second Reading Ukraine’s central bank will not support a crypto market bill that a parliamentary committee cleared for a final vote, warning that the draft leaves foreign tokens that act like electronic money outside its control and risks monetary sovereignty. The National Bank of Ukraine said in a Nov. 4 statement that Draft Law No. 10225-d on the circulation of virtual assets, recommended by the Verkhovna Rada Committee on Finance, Tax and Customs Policy for adoption in the second reading and as a whole, fails to reflect compromises struck during drafting. The NBU said it received the final text only late the evening before the committee vote and that the process “was not sufficiently transparent.” Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban raised the bank’s objections at the committee meeting, but the NBU said the format did not allow a full debate. Ukraine already legalized a framework for virtual assets in 2022. The new bill is meant to put that market under detailed rules modeled on the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, or MiCA, and on International Monetary Fund recommendations. The NBU says it supports that direction in principle. Three risks the NBU flags The bank’s public case rests on three points. First, the draft would let foreign tokens into Ukraine even when they function as electronic money but face no matching supervision in the countries where they are issued. That, the NBU said, threatens monetary sovereignty, the transmission of monetary policy, payment infrastructure and financial stability. The bank wants the same power it has over domestically issued tokens: the authority to assess those foreign assets and, when needed, restrict their circulation in Ukraine. Second, simplified admission of foreign virtual assets must not let them sidestep rules that apply to comparable Ukrainian assets. Without that parity, the NBU warned, segments of the market could expand outside adequate oversight and create regulatory arbitrage. Third, the bank flagged monopolization and corruption risks in how the National Securities and Stock Market Commission would authorize trading-platform operators. The NBU initially opposed numerical caps, then agreed as a compromise to limit the first wave to three legal persons chosen by competitive selection. The final draft, it said, drops a clear five-year cap and leaves the number of operators to the securities commission’s discretion without enough antitrust safeguards. What the bill would do next The committee’s Nov. 4 recommendation does not enact the law. A final Verkhovna Rada vote is expected later in November. If adopted, the rules would take effect on July 1, 2027, Interfax Ukraine reported , splitting supervision between the NBU and the securities commission. item.title: Fed and OCC Quiz U.S. Banks After $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Fed and OCC Quiz U.S. Banks After $6.3 Billion Binance Hack U.S. bank regulators contacted banks this week to check whether their systems had any vulnerabilities after last week’s $6.3 billion hack of Binance, Reuters reported Thursday, citing several people familiar with the matter. Supervisors from the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency began reaching out to banks on Monday morning, asking about any unusual activity or disruption in their services. The outreach shows regulators are treating the largest crypto theft on record as a possible risk to traditional finance, not just a problem for crypto exchanges, at a time when links between banks and the crypto industry have tightened. Banks run diagnostics One source at a bank that regulators contacted told Reuters there had been no disruptions to its services. Employees there prepared talking points for customers but have since received few inquiries. Banks have been studying the attack and running diagnostics on their own systems to make sure they could defend against something similar, two people familiar with the efforts said. Within hours of the hack, a cybersecurity team at one of the largest U.S. banks reached out to counterparts at Binance. That team is writing an internal report that will lead to a review of the bank’s systems and possibly cybersecurity updates. It was not yet clear whether the bank would be vulnerable to the same tactics. The biggest concern, one person said, is that artificial intelligence models have been evolving quickly, making it hard for banks to keep up with hackers. Banks are devoting a lot of resources to reviewing and patching their cybersecurity code. Binance said it was not aware of conversations between banks and regulators or whether the hack had any impact on U.S. banks. “We are in close contact with regulators all over the world, keeping them up to date on this security breach,” a Binance spokesperson said. How the Binance hack worked The concern about AI tracks with how the attack unfolded. Binance said the theft began with a fake job interview and ran for five months before any coins moved. The campaign combined a poisoned software download, a staged recruitment process, malware that evaded endpoint detection and an internal AI tool that the attackers turned against the company’s own wallet engineers. Funds began leaving Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. Blockchain analysis firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs linked the hack to TraderTraitor, a unit associated with North Korea. Binance reopened withdrawals in stages four days later, starting with bitcoin. It has said it froze or intercepted about $2.85 billion of the stolen assets and replenished 98% of affected tokens from its own funds. None of the techniques Binance described are unique to crypto. item.title: Tether and Tron Quietly Scrapped T3 Crime Unit Two Months Before $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Tether and Tron Quietly Scrapped T3 Crime Unit Two Months Before $6.3 Billion Binance Hack The T3 Financial Crime Unit, the anti-crime alliance Tron, Tether and TRM Labs launched in 2024 and later expanded to Binance, quietly shut down in late August, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, about two months before the record Binance hack. The alliance broke down over the past year amid slow response times and a lack of coordination among its members, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. One of them said T3 was terminated in late August. None of the companies announced the shutdown at the time. Tron, Tether and TRM confirmed that the initiative had wound down, without commenting on the details of the report. Binance declined to comment. “While the very successful T3 program has concluded, Tron remains committed to working to help stop illicit activities on the blockchain, in partnership with law enforcement,” a Tron DAO spokesperson said to Bloomberg . The spokesperson said Tron will share details of a new anti-crime initiative later. A Tether spokesperson said the company will keep working with TRM to disrupt illicit funds and has been taking part in Beacon Network, a real-time intelligence-sharing network TRM launched in August 2025. Tether is also working on the Financial Access and Systemic Empowerment Foundation, or FASE Foundation, which CEO Paolo Ardoino unveiled on X on Oct. 31. TRM’s global head of policy and government affairs, Ari Redbord, said “T3 achieved extraordinary things” and that “Beacon Network builds on that work.” What T3 was built to do Tron, Tether and TRM set up T3 in September 2024 as a public-private unit aimed at illicit use of Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the Tron blockchain. The pitch was speed. TRM supplied blockchain intelligence, Tron supplied network visibility and Tether supplied the power to freeze tokens at the issuer level. The unit said in August 2025 that it had frozen more than $250 million in illicit assets in less than a year. At the same time, it launched T3+, a program for outside partners, with Binance as its first member. Its first joint effort with the exchange froze almost $6 million tied to a pig-butchering scam. The totals kept climbing. TRM put the T3 tally above $300 million in February, when it announced a $70 million Series C round. In May, the unit announced that it had frozen more than $450 million and was working with authorities in 23 jurisdictions on five continents, including the U.S., Spain, Germany, Brazil and the U.K. That May release also said the unit had frozen funds within 24 hours of law enforcement requests in account takeovers and violent crime emergencies. It made no mention of the coordination problems Bloomberg has now described. TRM wrote that the Financial Action Task Force cited T3 in November 2025 guidance as a leading model for public-private enforcement work. item.title: Riot (RIOT) Names Anthropic as Tenant in $28 Billion Texas Lease, Could Owe It 12% Interest
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Riot (RIOT) Names Anthropic as Tenant in $28 Billion Texas Lease, Could Owe It 12% Interest Riot Platforms’ unnamed “Frontier AI Lab” is Anthropic, the bitcoin miner disclosed in its quarterly report filed Wednesday, naming the Claude developer as the tenant behind a 15-year lease worth about $28 billion on its Corsicana, Texas campus. The company’s results release on the same day described the tenant only as a “leading Frontier AI Lab.” The 10-Q is more specific. It says a Riot subsidiary signed the lease on Oct. 28 “with Anthropic PBC (the ‘Frontier AI Lab’),” and the deal became binding on Nov. 4 after Riot’s board approved it and outside consultants signed off on the technical specifications. The filing uses the same defined term for the tenant of Riot’s 191 MW Rockdale lease, signed in August. That makes Anthropic the counterparty on 1,101 MW of the 1,151 MW Riot has contracted. AMD holds the other 50 MW. The Corsicana lease covers 910 MW of critical IT capacity across the whole campus. Base rent starts at $130 per kilowatt per month and rises 3% a year. At that starting rate, the full 910 MW would bring in about $1.42 billion a year. Riot puts average annual rent at about $1.8 billion over the initial term, or roughly $54 billion in total if Anthropic exercises both five-year extensions. Riot’s 12% clause The detail drawing attention sits in the financing terms. The infrastructure company agreed to reimburse Anthropic up to $4 million per megawatt for the data center modules the tenant installs, or up to about $3.6 billion across the full 910 MW. That reimbursement depends on Riot raising money “on market terms reasonably acceptable to it.” If that financing is not available, the 10-Q says , Riot will instead give Anthropic rent credits that amortize the amount “plus interest at 12% per year” over the rest of the initial term. In that case, Anthropic would effectively finance the build itself and recover the cost out of rent at a double-digit rate. Riot’s base case is different. The company expects to fund the reimbursements with non-recourse project debt sized to the contracted rent, and it puts the total capital requirement at about $6 million per MW, or $5.5 billion. It said it does not currently expect to issue equity for the project. Deadlines and exits favor the tenant The lease puts most of the delivery risk on Riot. Capacity arrives in three phases: 400 MW with a first block targeted for June 28, 2027, 200 MW starting Dec. 24, 2027 and 310 MW on July 30, 2028. If Riot delivers more than 60 days late, Anthropic earns escalating rent credits capped at 270 days of base rent for the undelivered blocks. If a phase is not delivered within 270 days of its target, Anthropic can terminate the lease for that phase on 30 days’ notice, with extensions for force majeure of up to 365 days. item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $79,600 as Oil Rebounds and Bank of England Hikes Rates
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $79,600 as Oil Rebounds and Bank of England Hikes Rates Bitcoin price traded near $79,600 on Thursday morning, up about 2% from a day earlier but roughly $21,900 below its price one year ago, after slipping back under $80,000 as oil prices recovered and the Bank of England raised interest rates, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. Bitcoin changed hands at $79,632 at 8:05 a.m. ET, with a market cap of about $1.60 trillion and roughly $35.2 billion in trading volume over the past day. The move gives back a slice of Wednesday’s rally. Bitcoin price held near $80,000 through Wednesday afternoon and stayed above that level overnight, peaking just under $80,900 around 5 p.m. ET. It dipped below $80,000 in the 7 a.m. ET hour on Thursday, as stock futures turned mixed and oil firmed. The pullback is small next to the week’s swing. Bitcoin sat near $75,600 on election night, so Thursday’s price is still more than 5% above that low. Oil and rates set the tone Oil drove Wednesday’s relief rally, and it is now taking some of that back. Brent crude futures rose $1.53, or 1.6%, to $96.15 a barrel on Thursday, while West Texas Intermediate added 52 cents to $88.64. Both benchmarks fell more than 8% on Wednesday to settle at their lowest since Aug. 31. “The situation in the Middle East is still unresolved and that’s why there is some modest recovery in prices at the moment,” UBS commodity analyst Giovanni Staunovo said . That matters for the bitcoin price because energy has been the main channel from the Iran war into inflation and interest rates. Cheaper crude eases pressure on the Federal Reserve. A rebound does the opposite. The Bank of England made that link explicit on Thursday. Its Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate by a quarter point to 4%, its first hike in more than three years, with the one dissenter, Catherine Mann, pushing for a half-point move. The bank said U.K. inflation is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year, citing energy prices tied to a conflict “now in its ninth month.” CNBC called it the last major central bank to start tightening since the war began, a reminder that global rates are still moving against risk assets. Stocks cool, ETFs return U.S. stock futures split Thursday morning after the Dow’s best session since April 2025. Dow futures rose 0.5% and S&P 500 futures added 0.1%, while Nasdaq-100 futures dropped about 0.5% as chip and data center stocks stayed under pressure. Fund demand picked up. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $74.6 million on Wednesday, ending a three-session run of outflows that totaled about $1.16 billion. Fidelity’s FBTC drew $236.7 million, more than offsetting a $201.2 million outflow from BlackRock’s IBIT. Supply from miners remains a weight. item.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million American Bitcoin Corp. (Nasdaq: ABTC) reported about $126 million in third-quarter net income on Wednesday, a swing from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter that rested largely on a $197.3 million gain on the company’s bitcoin holdings rather than on mining revenue. The Miami-based miner and treasury company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp. and co-founded with Trump family backing, mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter at a cost of roughly $42,100 each and ended September with about 8,427 BTC. Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. Gross profit was about $25.8 million, a 41% margin, compared with about $33.0 million and 49% a quarter earlier, as seasonal power costs rose across its sites. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about $221 million, compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in the second quarter, according to the company’s release . Eric Trump, co-founder and chief strategy officer of American Bitcoin, said the quarter delivered the net income and Adjusted EBITDA figures while growing the bitcoin reserve and bitcoin per share. Chief Executive Mike Ho said the company kept mining at a structural discount to spot and raised satoshis per share by about 5% without issuing shares through its at-the-market program or buying bitcoin on the open market. A paper gain carried American Bitcoin’s quarter The income statement makes the driver plain. American Bitcoin booked a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in the third quarter, after a $71.2 million loss on that line in the second. Operating income was about $191.8 million. Other expense included a $64.3 million loss on derivatives. Strip the mark-to-market move out of the picture and the operating story looks quieter. Revenue per bitcoin mined was about $71,100, down slightly from about $71,900 in the second quarter, and the cost to mine rose to about $42,100 from about $36,500, the company said. Production of about 891 bitcoin was below the second quarter’s roughly 932 coins, which the company had called its highest quarterly haul on record when it reported a $57.2 million second-quarter loss alongside a climb in holdings to about 8,002 BTC. American Bitcoin said it sold a portion of production to cover operating costs while still adding to its strategic reserve. Holdings rose by about 425 bitcoin, or about 5%, to roughly 8,427 as of Sept. 30. That total includes about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under agreements with Bitmain. Reserve up, satoshis per share up Management’s preferred yardstick is satoshis per share, which rose about 5% to roughly 11,572 from about 10,989 at the end of June. The share count reflects a 1-for-15 reverse stock split effected earlier this year on July 2. The owned fleet stood at about 89,242 bitcoin miners with roughly 28.1 EH/s of capacity at quarter-end. item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority Stock perpetual futures can keep trading on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial for now after a federal judge denied an emergency bid to halt them Tuesday, while finding that the Wall Street-backed challengers are likely to prove the CFTC overstepped its authority. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges. The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford. The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges. Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms. “Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote. Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission. She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.” The request failed on one prong. Caproni said the declarations from Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets were “conjectural” about the harm members would suffer and did not show irreparable harm that was “actual and imminent.” What the ruling does and does not do The order leaves the approvals in place. It does not decide the case or the alliance’s separate motion for a preliminary injunction. The CFTC’s opposition is due Friday, Nov. 6, and the alliance’s reply is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. The order says that schedule is subject to change by the assigned judge. The docket lists Judge Lorna G. Schofield as assigned to the case. Kalshi was already listing four single-stock perps on Qualcomm, McDonald’s, Amgen and Costco by Wednesday morning, with maximum leverage of 4.9 times. Bloomberg Law reported that the judge signaled she might ultimately side with the Wall Street firms opposed to the products. A CFTC-SEC turf fight with crypto venues in the middle The fight is over a label. Selig’s Nov. 3 statement said the contracts were deemed approved under Commission Regulation 40.3 as security futures products, a category the CFTC and SEC oversee jointly.
